entities.text: AWAR D Kamal Kumar Thakur vs . Deepak Chauhan & Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
1. By this award, I shall decide a claim petition under section 166/140 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988,
filed by the petitioner - Kamal Kumar Thakur with respect to the injuries received by him in a motor vehicle accident.
2. The accident in the present case took place on 18.11.2015 in Noida.
It is the case of the petitioner that at around 10:00 PM, he was going to meet his brother Jitender Thakur at Surajpur from his car registration No. DL- 8CNV-7443.
His car got punctured.
He parked his car on the left side of the road for changing the wheel.

When he was changing the wheel of his car, a car (Honda City)
registration No.UP-16S-1290, driven by its driver respondent no. 1 Deepak Chauhan at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, hit him from back side.
Due to this accident, he sustained grievous injuries.
He was taken to ESI Hospital from where he was referred to Kailash Hospital.
He was discharged on the same day from the hospital.
A claim of Rs.5,00,000/- as compensation has been filed by the petitioner.
3. The respondent no. 1 Deepk Chauhan, the owner/driver of the offending vehicle did not choose to appear and reply to this claim.
4. The respondent no.2 Bajaj Allianze General Insurance Company Ltd / insurance company has taken the general defences.

entities.text: Bajaj Allianze General Insurance Company Ltd
entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text: The insurance company denied the accident and that the driver of the offending vehicle did not have the driving licence to drive the same.

5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties following issues were framed on 15.12.2020 : -
(i) Whether the petitioner Kamal Kumar Thakur suffered grievous injuries in a motor vehicular accident happened on 18.11.2015 at 10:00 p.m., on road in front of Botanical Garden, Noida, U.P., within the jurisdiction of PS Sector-20, Noida, due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle bearing registration no. UP16S-1290 (Honda City Car) by respondent no.1 Deepak Chauhan?

(OPP) 
(ii) Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation on account of said injuries and if yes, to what extent and from whom?

(OPP) 
(iii) Whether the petitioner is entitled to interest on the award amount, if so, at what rate and for which period?

(OPP)
(iv) Relief.
6. In order to establish his claim, petitioner Kamal Kumar Thakur has examined himself as PW-1.
The respondents have not led any evidence.
7. I have heard Mr. Bijay Kumar, counsel for petitioner and Mr. Sandeep Singh, counsel for respondent no.2- insurance company and perused the records.
8. The issues are decided as follows- Kamal Kumar Thakur vs . Deepak Chauhan & Another on 10 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98763812/

sentences.text:
2 ISSUE No.1 : Whether the petitioner Kamal Kumar Thakur suffered grievous injuries in a motor vehicular accident happened on 18.11.2015 at 10:00 p.m., on road in front of Botanical Garden,
Noida, U.P., within the jurisdiction of PS Sector-20, Noida, due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle bearing registration no. UP16S-1290 (Honda City Car) by respondent no.1 Deepak Chauhan? (OPP)
9.
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and in fact is the preponderance of probabilities which is applied in civil cases.
It is also the law that the tribunal is not bound by the technical rules of evidence.

Further in holding any inquiry under section 168, The Claims Tribunal may follow such summary procedure as it thinks fit.
10.
Now in this case, the petitioner Kamal Kumar Thakur is the injured and witness of the accident.

In order to establish his claim, he has examined himself as PW-1 and proved his aadhar card Ex.PW1/A, driving licence Ex.PW1/B, discharge summary/treatment record Mark-A, original medical bills Ex.PW1/C, original conveyance bill Ex.PW1/D and FIR Ex.PW1/E.
He stated on oath in the affidavit about the accident and how it was caused.
He has clearly deposed that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of the respondent no. 1, who was the driver of the car.
He has deposed that on 18.11.2015 in Noida, at around 10:00 PM, he was going to meet his brother Jitender Thakur at Surajpur from his car registration No. DL-8CNV-7443.
His car got punctured.
He parked his car on the left side of the road for changing the wheel.

When he was changing the wheel of his car, a car (Honda City) registration No. UP-16S-1290, driven by its driver respondent no. 1 Deepak Chauhan at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, hit him from back side.
Due to this accident, he sustained grievous injuries.
He was taken to ESI Hospital from where he was referred to Kailash Hospital.
He was discharged on the same day from the hospital.
He sustained injury in the form of laceration over nose, upper lip and left foot.
This is also reflected in his discharge summary.
He was doing private job in Delhi and used to earn Rs.20,000/- per month.

He has incurred Rs.15,000/- p.m. on his attendant, Rs.25,000/- on his medical treatment,
Rs.20,000/- each on special diet and conveyance.
11.
Respondent no.1 the owner/driver of the offending vehicle did not led any evidence to prove any contrary to the claim of the petitioner.

In the case of Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Cmpany Ltd vs Smt. Kamlesh and Others2009 (3) AD Delhi 310 it was held that an adverse inference can be drawn when the driver of the offending vehicle does not enter into the witness box.

entities.text: Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Cmpany Ltd vs Smt. Kamlesh and Others2009 (3) AD Delhi 310
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Even the insurance company has not led any evidence to disprove the claim of the petitioner.
12.

In view of above, on the basis of preponderance of probabilities of evidence and for filing of chargesheet, it is proved that the petitioner Kamal Kumar Thakur received injuries due to rash and negligent act of respondent no.1 Deepak Chauhan, the driver of the offending vehicle.

Accordingly,
this issue is decided in favour of the petitioner and against the respondents.
ISSUE No.2 : Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation on account of said injuries and if yes, to what extent and from whom?

sentences.text: Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
The compensation should not be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
14. The case of Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343, is one of the most prominent judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court which deals with compensation in injuries cases.

entities.text: Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It was held in this case that in routine personally injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under the heads - (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalisation, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.
(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured ,
comprising (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment and (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.

Now, in the present case, there is no record to show that the petitioner Kamal Kumar Thakur had suffered grievous injuries in the accident and therefore, it is considered that his injuries were simple in nature.
Considering it as a case of routine personal injury, the compensation is awarded to him under the aforesaid heads as follows -

MEDICAL EXPENSES:
15.
Petitioner has stated in his evidence affidavit that he has incurred Rs.25,000/- on his medical treatment.
The petitioner has proved medical bills Ex.PW1/C (colly).

These bills are of Rs.18,341/-
collectively.
Under this head the actual medical bills are reimbursed.

Therefore, I award Rs.18,341/-
as medical expenses to the petitioner.

PAIN AND SUFFERING:
16.
As per medical documents, the petitioner has suffered simple injuries in the present case.
Considering the nature of injury, I find it appropriate to grant a sum of Rs.25,000/- to the petitioner under this head.
LOSS OF INCOME DURING TREATMENT :
17. Petitioner has claimed he was doing private job in Delhi at the time of accident and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Therefore, there is no evidence for how long the petitioner was unable to work or what was the consequential loss of income to him due to this injury.
Because the injury was simple, therefore, no compensation can be granted under this head.

18. Thus, the compensation awarded to the petitioner is summarized as under:-
 Sl. No. Head of compensation Amount  1. Medical Expenses Rs.18,341 /-
 2. Pain & Sufferings Rs.25,000/-
 TOTAL Rs.43,341/-

sentences.text: In his reply filed by the respondent no. 2, insurance company, it is stated that respondent no., 1 did not have the driving licence on the date of accident and that there was a breach of insurance policy.
The driver of the offending vehicle Deepak Chauhan had not joined the proceedings or placed on record his driving licence.
The burden to prove the fact that he had a valid driving licence was upon the driver Deepak Chauhan in the light of all other evidence against him which he failed to discharge.
He has not even appeared as a witness to prove that he had the licence on that day.
Therefore, adverse inference can be drawn against him.
Therefore, all these things clearly indicate and proves that respondent no. 1 Deepak Chauhan was not holding the valid driving licence at the time of accident.
20. Now, the question arises as to which of the respondents are liable to pay the compensation amount.
As insurance company has contractual and statutory liability to indemnify the insured.

Counsel for insurance company has raised the issue of recovery rights against the respondent no.1 who was the owner and driver of the offending vehicle on the ground that the driver Deepak Chauhan was not having a valid driving licence.
Deepak Chauhan has failed to prove his licence entitling thereby entitling the insurance company to recover the compensation amount from him.

RELIEF:
21.

In view of the findings on above points, I as presiding officer of this Tribunal award a total compensation of Rs.43,341/- (Rs. Forty Three Thousand, Three Hundred & Forty-One only) along with interest @ 6% per annum on the aforesaid award amount from the date of accident till realization in favour of petitioner against the respondent no.2, insurance company/ Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd.

sentences.text: This award is required to be deposited with this Tribunal within 30 days.
